title: ward backup writes a file that restore will refuse when the state document does not parse
description:
Filed from the WCLI-51 independent review as work discovered outside that task acceptance criteria, and from the residual recorded when WCLI-49 was closed as moot under DEC-38.

runBackup in src/application/backup.ts opens and authenticates the envelope through store.read, then seals the resulting plaintext into the backup container WITHOUT PARSING IT. Envelope authentication means a damaged or foreign vault is refused before a backup exists, which is why the WCLI-49 asymmetry dissolved. But a plaintext that decrypts and does not parse still backs up: backup exits 0 and writes a durable file that ward restore will then refuse.

Under DEC-38 that is no longer a format case, because Ward has a single format. It is a defect in the backup path: the command output invites a reader to treat the file as recovery material, and this build cannot honour it. The DEC-38 residual recorded in the WCLI-49 closure says no task covers it; this is that task.

Reachability today is low and that is not a reason to leave it untracked. It is filed because ADR 0010 now states the gap explicitly, and a stated gap with no task behind it is how a recorded limitation becomes an unrecorded one.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The behaviour of ward backup on a plaintext that does not parse is decided and recorded, rather than left as it is by default
The command output can no longer invite a reader to treat such a file as recovery material this build cannot honour
A test pins the answer against a vault whose plaintext decrypts and fails to parse

plan: Refuse in runBackup: parse the plaintext after store.read and before the KDF, seal and file-create, answering vault_state_malformed with no file written
Pin it in test/backup.test.ts with a raw-document fixture: refusal and no file for a document that does not parse, and a same-fixture control that a parseable document still backs up
Record the decision and its cost in ADR 0010s consequences bullet via lore, replacing the gap sentence that goes false
Sweep the application layer for any other site that consumes a snapshot without parsing it, and record what was measured
Run the full check, open the PR, close WCLI-52 in it with the measurement recorded
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED on fix/WCLI-52-backup-unreadable-state. DECISION (opum-agent ruled this component design, i.e. this repository to make, with the record here rather than in opum-doc): refuse, and write no file. runBackup parses the plaintext after store.read and before the KDF, the seal and files.create, answering vault_state_malformed. ADR 0010 consequences bullet updated from the gap sentence that would otherwise have gone false.

MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX (on 908c15a, vault created as store.create(vaultId, key, "{not a state document")): ward backup --output <path> --json exited 0 and wrote a 349-byte file; ward restore of that file exited 6 with vault_state_malformed and created nothing. The success text promises "recovery from a lost key or a damaged vault needs this file and its passphrase".

PROOF, both halves. With the fix: test/backup.test.ts 18/18 green, including the new WCLI-52 describe (both shapes of unparseable document refused with no file and no success text, plus a same-construction control whose file is written AND restores). With the parse stashed back out of src/application/backup.ts: exactly the new refusal case fails (1 of 18) while the control still passes, which localises the failure to the parse rather than the fixture.

SWEEP, measured rather than asserted. Every other consumer of a snapshot plaintext in src/application parses it: reporting.ts:219, project.ts:149 and :285, secrets.ts:182, profiles.ts:162, audit.ts:137, run.ts:113. Every store.mutate callback parses before use: project.ts:156 via stateOf, secrets.ts:251 and :304, profiles.ts:429, run.ts:194. setup.ts:58 reads to prove the key opens the vault and discards the bytes; it produces no artifact a later reader refuses, so it is a different object. runBackup was the only site with this shape.

COST, recorded in ADR 0010: preserving the bytes of a damaged vault means copying the vault file, not taking a Ward backup.

CHECKS: bun run check green (typecheck, lint 3 pre-existing warnings, format, layers 47 files 0 violations, evals OK, 648 tests 0 fail); lore check exit 0 (13 files).
